transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on things like I used to. At work I’ll be looking at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I’ll realize I’ve read the same line three or four times and still haven’t taken it in. Then I put off making calls because even simple decisions feel harder than they should.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yes. Most days I feel this dull heaviness, like it’s just sitting on me. Even when I’m doing things that used to help, like going to the community center or working in my garden, I’m sort of just going through the motions and trying to keep a smile on.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I still do some of those things, but I don’t know if I’d say I enjoy them the way I used to. It’s more like I’m there, doing them, but it doesn’t feel like much.
How have you been sleeping lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping close track of it. Some nights feel better than others, but I don’t know that I could say exactly what’s changed.
Did anything particularly stressful happen around the time these problems with concentration and mood began?
Yes… it really seemed to start after my close friend died. That was a little over two years ago now, and I don’t feel like I’ve been the same since.
Do thoughts about your friend’s death still feel like the main thing driving how you’ve been feeling?
I think so, yes. It’s been going on since my close friend died, a little over two years ago. That still feels like where it started.
Do you still find yourself yearning for or strongly longing for your friend?
I’m not sure I’d call it yearning, exactly. I do miss my friend, of course, but I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Do thoughts about your friend take over your mind a lot, even when you’re trying to focus on something else?
I’m not sure. I think about my friend sometimes, but I don’t know that it really takes over my mind a lot. I haven’t paid attention to it that way.
Have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself a lot lately?
I’m not really sure. I do get down on myself sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say I feel worthless or that I’m blaming myself a lot.
Do thoughts about your friend’s death keep coming back into your mind even when you don’t want them to?
I don’t really know. I mean, I do think about it sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it coming back into my mind when I don’t want it to, not in a way I could clearly say.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?
I haven’t really noticed a big change. My appetite seems about the same, I think.
Since your friend died, have you felt like a part of who you are is missing?
I’m not sure. I miss them, of course, but I don’t know that I’d say a part of who I am is missing. I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Have you had any medical illness or head injury around the time these concentration problems began?
Not that I can think of. I don’t remember having any illness or head injury around when the concentration problems started.
During the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yes. Most days I’ve had this kind of dull heaviness with me. Even when I’m doing things that used to help, like going to the community center or working in my garden, I feel like I’m just going through the motions and putting on a smile.
During the past two weeks, have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed it clearly. Some things still matter to me, but I can’t say for sure how much pleasure I’m getting from them lately.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to?
I’m not really sure. I do worry about things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being a lot of different things for no reason. It’s hard for me to say.
If your friend had not died, do you think these problems with your mood and concentration would still be happening?
I think so, yes. It really started after my close friend died, a little over two years ago, and it’s just kind of stayed with me since then.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual lately?
I haven’t really noticed that. I don’t think anyone’s said I’m moving or talking slower than usual, at least not that I can remember.
During the past two weeks, have you been feeling tired or low on energy nearly every day?
Yes. Most days I wake up tired even if I slept the whole night. And after just a couple of client calls, or something simple like watering the tomatoes, I feel like my body’s already done a full day.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself?
I don’t really have anything specific to tell you there. I mean… I don’t think about hurting myself.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient confirms a depressive mood most days over the past two weeks, reduced pleasure/engagement in previously enjoyable activities, fatigue/low energy, and impaired concentration/indecisiveness, with functional difficulties at work. Although symptoms began after the death of a close friend, the interview does not establish core prolonged grief features or clear anxiety predominance, and no medical illness or head injury supports an organic etiology. The presentation is therefore most consistent with a depressive episode, unspecified severity.
